seo_description: DisplayLayoutKeeper is a free, open-source menu bar app that remembers window positions for each monitor setup and restores them when displays change.
hero_sub: DisplayLayoutKeeper saves window positions for each monitor setup and restores them when you dock, undock or wake your Mac. It lives in the menu bar; Save Now is ⌘S, Restore Now is ⌘R.
features_sub: Everything runs locally, with no accounts, servers or telemetry.

features.title: A layout per monitor setup
features.desc: Each arrangement is identified by every display's UUID, pixel size and position, so layouts survive port changes.

features.title: Automatic snapshots
features.desc: Windows are saved every 60 seconds by default (10 to 600), once the setup has been stable for 5 seconds, and again just before sleep.

features.title: Restore when displays change
features.desc: After a configurable delay (3 seconds by default), windows return to their saved frames. Positions are clamped onto the nearest connected display.

features.title: Smart window matching
features.desc: Windows match by app bundle ID and exact title, then fall back to window index. That keeps browser windows with changing tab titles in place.

features.title: Exclude apps you choose
features.desc: Pick apps from /Applications that should never be saved or moved. Launch at login and auto-restore are simple toggles in Settings.

features.title: Private and local
features.desc: Layouts are stored as JSON files on your Mac, capped at 20 configurations. Screen Recording is not requested.

permissions_step: When prompted, grant Accessibility access in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility; notifications are optional.

faq.q: Is DisplayLayoutKeeper free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is free and released under the MIT license, with the full source on GitHub. If it saves you some headaches, you can support development through the Ko-fi link in the app.

Accessibility is required so the app can read window titles, positions and sizes and move windows on restore. Notifications are optional and used only for a short confirmation after an automatic restore. It does not ask for Screen Recording, Camera or Microphone.
Only on your Mac, in Application Support under DisplayLayoutKeeper/Snapshots, as one JSON file per monitor configuration. Nothing is sent anywhere, and you can delete any saved layout from the menu.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, which this free project does not have. Right-click the app and choose Open once to approve it, or build it yourself from source with Xcode.
